findings.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? executes an uncached DB query (where("lower(host) = ?", host).first) on every /embed/comments request, replacing the previously process-cached SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? check, so database load now scales linearly with embedding traffic on the highest-QPS embed route; needs a cached lookup invalidated on admin CRUD or at minimum request-level memoization

The embeddable_hosts table is created with no index on host and no uniqueness constraint, and since the lookup queries lower(host), a plain index on host would not be used — it requires a functional (ideally unique) index on lower(host) or normalizing to lowercase on write plus a unique index; the missing unique constraint also permits duplicate rows that make .first nondeterministic

The migration crashes with NoMethodError for sites that never set embed_category, because execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'] is called on an empty result set (site-setting defaults are not persisted as rows), aborting db:migrate and blocking deploys for most upgrading installs
The migration's INSERT statement interpolates '#{h}' unescaped, so a quote character in a legacy host value breaks the SQL

expandable_first_post? in app/models/topic.rb removed the free SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard that short-circuited the has_topic_embed? per-topic DB lookup, so with embed_truncate enabled the DB check now runs during topic rendering even on installs with no embedding configured

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? executes an uncached DB query (where("lower(host) = ?", host).first) on every /embed/comments request, replacing the previously process-cached SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? check, so database load now scales linearly with embedding traffic on the highest-QPS embed route; needs a cached lookup invalidated on admin CRUD or at minimum request-level memoization

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the embed access check from an in-memory SiteSetting-based whitelist (SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?) to EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer) (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb, lib/topic_retriever.rb). EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? calls record_for_host, which parses the URL then executes an ActiveRecord query `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). There is no caching or memoization shown, so this introduces a database query on every /embed/comments request where the check runs, which is a verifiable performance regression compared to the previous string check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The embeddable_hosts table is created with no index on host and no uniqueness constraint, and since the lookup queries lower(host), a plain index on host would not be used — it requires a functional (ideally unique) index on lower(host) or normalizing to lowercase on write plus a unique index; the missing unique constraint also permits duplicate rows that make .first nondeterministic

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with only columns and timestamps—no index on `host` and no uniqueness constraint. The model also lacks `validates :host, uniqueness: ...`. Lookup is done via `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so duplicates are allowed and `.first` will pick an arbitrary matching row (potentially the wrong `category_id` for `TopicEmbed.import`, which uses `eh.try(:category_id)`). Additionally, even if an index on `host` were later added, this query form would generally require a functional index on `lower(host)` (or normalization to lowercase on write) to be index-friendly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The migration's INSERT statement interpolates '#{h}' unescaped, so a quote character in a legacy host value breaks the SQL

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the loop does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` where `h` comes from the legacy `site_settings.value` for `embeddable_hosts` split by newlines. This interpolates `h` directly into a single-quoted SQL literal without escaping/quoting via the connection, so a legacy host value containing a single quote would produce invalid SQL (and more generally is unsafe string construction).

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? in app/models/topic.rb removed the free SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard that short-circuited the has_topic_embed? per-topic DB lookup, so with embed_truncate enabled the DB check now runs during topic rendering even on installs with no embedding configured

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. That removal eliminates an early short-circuit that previously avoided evaluating `has_topic_embed?` when embedding wasn’t configured. Since embedding configuration has moved from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` to the `EmbeddableHost` table (and no replacement guard like `EmbeddableHost.exists?` was added), enabling `embed_truncate` can now cause `has_topic_embed?` to be evaluated for topics even when there are zero allowed embeddable hosts. If `has_topic_embed?` triggers an association/database check (likely for a `TopicEmbed`), this is a real performance regression introduced by the diff.
